exercises.title: 1. Cold start
exercises.description: Capture where your voice arrives on its own. Do not correct or warm up before this take.

steps.label: Count from 1 to 20 and speak spontaneously for a few seconds with the voice that showed up today.

exercises.title: 2. Weight foundation
exercises.description: Separate weight from pitch. Explore comfortably and keep volume moderate.

steps.label: On the same comfortable note, slowly alternate between a heavier sound and a lighter sound.
Glide gently upward and allow the sound to become lighter; descend without restoring all the weight.
Find a light, clean sound without excess air and count from 1 to 10 while maintaining the weight.

exercises.title: 3. Vocal size
exercises.description: Explore vocal-tract space before carrying the movement into speech.

steps.label: With an unvoiced /eh/, slide from a large space to a small space and back.
Use gentle unvoiced /puh/ pulses to find and repeat the smaller adjustment without squeezing.
Begin on /m/, open into a vowel, and maintain the smaller size through the transition.
Move slowly through /ee ih eh ah aw oh oo/ while keeping the same overall size scale.

exercises.title: 4. Fullness map
exercises.description: Small size pairs with light weight; large size pairs with heavy weight. Explore the map without chasing force or tension.

steps.label: Gently visit all four corners of the map and place the target where your desired voice seems to live.
Start from a hollow sound: keep the weight light and reduce size until the sound gains fullness.
Start from a buzzy sound: keep the size small and reduce weight until it balances.
Travel along the large/heavy to small/light diagonal and back without leaving the full region.

exercises.title: 5. Integration
exercises.description: Carry the coordination into progressively larger units of speech.

steps.label: Count, say the days of the week, and ask three questions while keeping size and weight coordinated.
Read a paragraph and then summarize it in your own words without looking at the feedback.

exercises.title: 6. Recall
exercises.description: Step away for a few minutes, speak normally, and try to recover the coordination without a long setup.

steps.label: Hide feedback, recover your target voice from memory, and count from 1 to 20.
Speak spontaneously for one minute. Prioritize an easy, stable recall rather than a perfect position.
